title: Encoder
body:
[[Priority Encoder]]

The inverse of a [[Decoder]]: $2^n$ inputs in, $n$ outputs out. Exactly one input is
expected to be high, and the encoder outputs its index in binary.

| $I_3 I_2 I_1 I_0$ | Out |
|:-:|:-:|
| 0001 | 00 |
| 0010 | 01 |
| 0100 | 10 |
| 1000 | 11 |

The catch is the assumption. Two inputs high at once and a plain encoder ORs the two
answers together into a third index that is wrong for both. A [[Priority Encoder]] fixes
that by ranking the inputs, which is what makes it the useful one in practice.
